newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Under 1/3 gold stocks for lending - RepublicNat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Under 1/3 gold stocks for lending - RepublicNat.

text.p: Less than a third of total central bank holdings of gold are potentially available for lending to the market, according to a senior Sydney-based official of Republic National Bank of New York.

Central bank and offical gold holdings amount to about 35,000 tonnes, Lester Solden, Republic National's senior vice president and director, central bank sector trading, says in a paper to be delivered at a conference here on Wednesday.
"However ... breakdown of the stocks suggest that no more than 10,000 tonnes are potentially available for lending to the market," Solden said.

Eighty percent of that amount is held by countries already participating in the market "which leaves only a modest proportion of total stocks of gold as yet untapped," Solden said in the paper to be delivered at the Outlook 97 commodities conference in Canberra.
Solden said many believe that because much of the gold not in the market is widely dispersed or not in good form for delivery, it may be inaccessible.

"There are still many countries which hold their (gold) reserves in their own central banks and the prospect of them being seen to physically move gold in the streets to their airports for shipping to traditional market centres is more than many politicians can bear to think about," Solden said.
Solden estimates that between 60 and 70 central banks worldwide currently provide gold to the market, the main attraction being a modest return on otherwise dormant assets.
"During 1997, it is reasonable to expect that some large scale holders of gold reserves will cast off their shackles and begin lending gold to the market," Solden said.
"I fully anticipate that this will include countries with both traditional as well as relatively newly created holdings," he said.
